They glared at each other, Zuko’s embarrassment roiling into fury as Katara matched him, maybe even surpassing Zuko’s own anger.

“You *tricked* us,” Katara reminded him, “like some… you tricked my brother. “We thought-someone had *come back* but it was- and you know what? When I think about the worst things you’ve done? That’s not even in the *worst*. You’re a…. *horrible* person and I can’t- I don’t… *see* it.”

Zuko frowned at her. His mind raced, trying to think of… *anything*. “It wouldn’t have *worked*,” Zuko told her harshly, “if the Avatar had told you I’d rescued him at the Pohuai Stronghold.”

Katara scowled, “Are you saying this *is* Aang’s fault?!”

That definitely *wasn’t* the point Zuko *wanted* to make. In fact, he wasn’t exactly sure what he *was* trying to say. “I-" he hesitated. “Found the bison.”

Katara, still glaring, gave him a nod. “Yes,” she said stiffly, her looped hair bobbing by her chin, “you *did*.”

“It wasn’t…” Zuko felt his inner fire simpering down. He wished more than anything it *wouldn’t* . It was much easier to match anger with anger, though if he took any stock in his *dreams* - and he didn’t want to - then he probably *shouldn’t*. “I didn’t… plan any of it.”

“An *accident*, then,” Katara asked him, “you’re blaming it on an *accident*.”

“I’m not *blaming* anyone but myself!” Zuko shouted, “I’m just *explaining*!”

“Explain *better*!” Katara demanded, “Why did you *do* everything you did, especially *lately*? Why did Sokka forgive you so quickly when you- you *weren’t there*, you didn’t see how *miserable* he was because of what *you* put him through! I was the *only* one,” her mouth trembled, “I was the only one he told, the only one who knew, and I was trying to help him but I couldn’t- I just… I wanted to meet you again so I could *fight you* and make you *pay* and then…” her eyes dropped to Zuko’s stomach.

Zuko wasn’t sure how good his response of '*I was miserable too'* was, if it would help or if it just made it all about himself, so he swallowed it down and didn’t answer.

“Your sister did this,” Katara said, her voice suddenly quiet. The shift was enough to nearly make Zuko’s head spin. “Why.”

“I don’t know,” Zuko said, not lying on purpose but the more he thought about it the more he realized it wasn’t true. “I… *guess…* ” he frowned, turning his head to look at the ice stuck to the wall to avoid looking at her, “after the North Pole she had orders to take me and my uncle back home. As prisoners. But we, thanks to Uncle Iroh, we escaped.” His fingers, absent-minded, lightly traced the edges of his new scar. “Then I think she promised our father she could do better. Bring him the Avatar. I’m rather surprised she *didn’t,* it- it wouldn’t have surprised me.”

“I think *you* of all people should know it’s not that easy to beat *us* ,” Katara reminded him.

“Everything is easy for her.” Zuko forced back a sigh. “Even if she gave him Ba Sing Se, she still hadn’t done what she must have promised to do*.* Even if she handed the capital of the Earth Kingdom to him… our father doesn’t appreciate *faults* in his machine. You have to be perfect. Always. But…” He swallowed, his right index finger stilling on the scar and pressing down, just slightly, just enough to feel the ache on his wound to distract him from the one building in his chest. “Father can change his mind, or be *distracted*, so, if she fulfilled her *original goal* then… our father might be amused enough to forget.”

Katara hummed in understanding. “So you… understand why she did it. Aren’t you- I’d have thought you’d be furious.”

“I’m…” Zuko *isn’t*. He knows that. He probably should be- he *definitely* should be… “She’s my little sister, it’s complicated.”

“Fine.” Katara sat back down with a sigh. “I get why the Fire Nation would want your uncle prisoner, *he* helped us at the North Pole. *Not* you. You were… *ugh*.”

Zuko didn’t feel like turning back to look at her. For the second time he really wished she’d sat on his other side so avoiding her gaze would be easier.

“Why you?” Katara asked sourly, “All you ever did was be a jerk and try to *capture* Aang.”

“But I… didn’t,” Zuko reminded her.

“No.” Katara said, her voice fierce, “You *didn’t*.”

He didn’t. Zuko sighed now, unable to help it, and lifted his hand from his stomach. He forced himself to turn his head, to meet Katara’s eyes with his.

She and Sokka looked so much alike, the same skin, same nose, same bright blue eyes like the ocean that blinked back at him. The same way they stared, eyebrows furrowed and mouth drawn tight, angry but also *open*. Zuko wondered if people had ever thought the same about him and Azula.

“I guess you *are* on our side now,” Katara mused, “it’s not like anyone could *fake* being that close to…” *Death* . She didn’t seem willing to say the word. At least not to Zuko’s face.

“Can I ask something?” Zuko asked her.

Katara nodded.

“Where am I?”

Katara grinned at him and shrugged. “In a Fire Nation ship.”

“I *know* that,” Zuko told her, annoyed, “*why*.”

“Why not?” Katara said, standing up. She raised her arms over her head with a groan, stretching. “I promised to tell everyone when you were awake enough to talk.” She dropped her hands to her hips. “Are you?”

“Yes.”

“Well, good,” Katara shrugged. “I’ll go get them.”

“Them? Sokka?” Zuko asked her.

She squinted, frowning down at him. “*Everyone*,” she said curtly, “you’ve been asleep for almost two weeks.”

“Who’s everyone?” Zuko asked her, and then immediately after, “A *week*?”

“*Over* a week,” Katara said. She walked down the room, over to the desk, and opened a drawer. Then she pulled out something red. “Here.” Katara threw the object at Zuko, who tried to raise a hand to catch it in time but missed. It was cloth though, and it fell gently onto his shoulder.

“What’s-" Zuko started to ask.

“A shirt,” Katara told him. “And Toph and Aang.”

Zuko picked the cloth up, wincing as he forced himself to sit up enough to be separated from the blankets. “*What*?”

Katara shrugged. “Everyone wants to see you.”

“Why?” Zuko asked nervously.

Katara walked over to the door, frowning. She stopped when she reached it, one hand on the doorframe, and sighed. “*Because*,” she said, still with a trace of anger, “I guess you’re one of us now.”

Zuko looked down at the red tunic in his hands and swallowed. “*Right*,” he realized, “I guess I am.”

“It’s weird, isn’t it?” Katara asked.

“Definitely,” Zuko agreed. He met her eyes as she turned her head to look at him, frowning with more curiosity than anger now, it seemed. “Thank you,” Zuko told her, “for not letting me die.”

Katara’s eyes widened for a moment and then she scowled. “Just- just put on the shirt!” She turned, sharply, back to the door and walked out quickly. Zuko could hear her feet stomping as she walked down the hall.

He was one of them, a rebel, Zuko thought, his eyes falling to the red tunic in his hands; not the same though, he was a traitor too. Him and his uncle. Going to fight his father, defeat the Fire Lord. And Sokka was coming to see him.

Raising his arms, and wincing as he did, Zuko slipped on the shirt.

## Chapter 25: A Beginning
