### Text

It was definitely a mistake to look in the mirror. Zuko just hadn’t been *expecting* there to be one in this bathroom; his old ship hadn’t had a private lavatory like this, and regardless of that he’d never seen any in the bathrooms he’d used that he could recall. For a military ship, it was a little pointless to place something so fragile up against a wall - whoever captained this ship previously must have been vain. Consequences of which meant Zuko raised his head after splashing his face with the waterbasin and was forced to see himself.

He cursed under his breath. Zuko had no idea how much time he had, one hand was currently just leaning on the basin to help him stay standing, he didn’t know what he *could* do about the way he looked right now. Sallow cheeks, dark circles under his eye, and shamelessly ragged hair. With his one free hand, he used the water to attempt to push his hair into any kind of order, and down on the back where it was sticking up slightly where his head had met the pillow. “F…” Zuko mumbled, rubbing his thumb over his only eyebrow and then vigorously under his eye, “*fuck*.” Katara could have given him a *little* more time, just as a sign of good faith, right? At least a day to try to fix the only parts of his face he could improve. Or a tunic that didn’t hang so loose around his neck.

Zuko was still royal by *birth*, he had grown up enduring having his hair done every morning, wearing tailored clothing with gold stitching, shoes made of the finest leathers that had been cured for months from the best artisans, owning jewelry older than the caldera itself - he used to *look like* *a prince*, once, and yet every time he met Sokka he seemed to get progressively more disheveled and… *worse*. He sighed, used his free right hand to tuck some of his hair behind his right ear, used his nails to push as much of his hair on his left over his eye, and glared at his appearance. As if he could use sheer will to force himself look nicer.

“Great.” Zuko turned head down toward his feet by the door to glare at the little creature watching him. Momo chirped and tilted his head. “*What*?” Zuko asked the lemur sourly.

Zuko’s hand shook on the basin as he tried to keep himself standing. It hadn’t been the best idea to walk on his own, he was already feeling lightheaded, but he had to at least… clean up, do *something*. Momo pounced away from the doorframe as Zuko returned his gaze again to the reflection. He took in a breath. Exhaled out warm air. Did it again.

He was *alive*. That was a good thing. Obviously. Iroh was alive, and nearby, which also - Zuko blinked and kept his eyes shut for a moment - was a good thing. Sokka was not his *enemy* anymore, which was a definite step upward.

Zuko opened his eyes and, after a moment, saw red by his side. His hands still on the basin, he had to turn his whole head over to see.

Momo was chattering beside two spike-toed shoes, as if giving a nonsense report to an armor clad soldier in full regalia standing in the center of the room. *Ill-fitting* regalia, the breeches were stuffed haphazardly into the boots and the armor seemed to slip and lean on one of the shoulders, not too obvious, in fact perfectly acceptable, but certainly a display of disarray that *Zuko* had *never* tolerated on his own ship.

The first thing Zuko thought, upon seeing a Fire Nation soldier standing in his room, was to order him to fetch him some shoes. A moment later, his brain caught up to what was happening. There shouldn’t be a soldier here, in disguise, or even having entered this room without knocking, he was on a Fire Navy ship, with his uncle, and Katara… it was a capture. Disguise. Also, he should probably find a way to remind himself that he was *the enemy*. His first instinct at the sight of a Fire Nation soldier should now be to *run*, not give him orders.

There was a lot to take in. Zuko shook his head. “The armor plating goes on before the fastenings,” Zuko said simply, “to adjust to varying sizes.”

“Oh,” the Navy-uniform wearing figure said, with a voice slightly distorted by the metal plate but still *distinctly* Sokka’s.

“Technically you aren’t regulation height either,” Zuko said, doing his absolute best not to raise his hand to double check his hair.

Sokka lifted a hand to the helmet and took it off all at once, the faceplate still attached. He frowned, but grinned a moment later.

Zuko couldn’t help but smile back at him. It was a weird sight, Sokka with his Water Tribe wolftail wearing red clothing and armor, in the middle of the room as casual as could be. He couldn’t say he liked the sight of the uniform on him, it was far too strange, but Sokka’s face smiling back? That was…

He gripped the basin tight with his right hand so he could turn, still supported and standing. “There’s a strict code of uniformity with nondomestic forces,” Zuko continued, “for the unspecialized navy, at least.” He instantly regretted it, as Sokka raised an eyebrow, lifted his other hand to run through his loose wolf tail and *looked* at him; Zuko should have thought of *anything* else to talk about. ‘Guess I’m alive? Nice to see you. How have things been? I had a weird conversation with your sister’ - literally *anything* would have been better than *Fire Nation navy* *regulations*.

“Hm,” Sokka looked down at himself for only a moment before lifting his head back up to grin at Zuko, “I think I pull it off.”

“*Pull* it off?” Zuko asked.

Sokka made some kind of motion, probably a shrug, which caused the armor to click by his shoulder. “What? I think I make one good-looking jerk in armor,” he said brightly, “though I have to say, not at *all* a fan of the boots. I can’t even feel my feet.”

Zuko wasn’t wearing shoes, the metal was cold, he was in loose pants and a loose tunic like a peasant or a… patient. He didn’t want to think about what *Sokka* was seeing, but Sokka himself, “You look,” Zuko said, swallowing down whatever feeling was building up at the bottom of his throat, “better in blue.”

“Ah,” Sokka said. He raised a hand to the back of his neck. “That’s probably best. I mean I, I do *wear* blue. Most of the time.”

“You *are* from the water tribes,” Zuko reminded him lamely.

“I am,” Sokka said, blinking at him, “I, yes. From the water tribes. Sokka.”

“Yes.”

“Huh.” Sokka tucked the helmet under his arm and looked at Zuko curiously. “Did you really recognize me right away?”

“No,” Zuko admitted, “not until you spoke.”

Sokka, for some reason, smiled so brightly at Zuko he was practically beaming. “The voice *always* gives it away,” he said. Then he raised his free hand to his face, and made a gesture that Zuko, this time, understood. *Jerk*, Sokka had signed.

It was so nice to be there, next to him, even *here*, although Zuko never really did seem to meet Sokka under ideal circumstances… except for the *once* , in the clearing behind the library. Even then, it hadn’t been - with the mask, and Zuko planning to *betray* him, it had been wrong. Never perfect.

Sokka coughed. “So uh…” he gestured vaguely at Zuko, “I didn’t think you’d be standing, that’s great! Great. Definitely.”

Zuko clenched the basin tighter, realizing now would be the most embarrassing time to fall over. “Thank you,” he said.

Sokka blinked at him.

Zuko, his mind spinning so fast trying to think of something *right* to say, came up with absolutely nothing coherent and stared back.

A crash to his left made Zuko flinch. There was a loud noise that had Zuko nearly lose his grip, as the door to the room that was already open anyway swung open and hit the wall with a bang. Dressed in green with a wide grin on her face, Toph, the earthbender jumped into the room and stepped right over to Zuko. “Sparky!” She yelled.

Zuko frowned at her. “What?”

“That’s you,” Toph said, raising a hand to his arm like she was going to punch him. Her knuckles only pressed into his arm though, a pale imitation of a hit.

“Hey! Careful!” Sokka said from behind her, rushing to put the helmet down on the desk before walking up close.

“I *was* careful!” Toph said indignantly. “Right, Sparky?”

Zuko frowned down at her. “Are you… do you mean me?” He asked.

“What else am I going to call you?” Toph asked him, smirking, “Your Royal Highness, Crown Prince of the Fire Nation, son of Fire Lord Ozai, firstborn heir and first of his name? Gross.”

“Uh, what?” Sokka asked.

“Kind of a mouthful,” Toph pointed out.

“I suppose it is,” Zuko said. If he could have shrugged, he would have.

“So, Sparky,” Toph decided.

“I guess-“ Zuko started to say, when the interruption of a familiar, angry voice cut him off.

“Why is he *out of bed*?!” Katara yelled.

---

It had seemed vitally important that they all ate in the same room, with Zuko. Katara arrived with two bowls of steaming jook, and Aang following her with three, and immediately handed them out while scowling at Zuko until he made his way back to the bed. It was easier to return, considering Sokka immediately put an arm on his waist and helped support him as he did.

So Zuko was resting back on the bed, the furs behind his back to support his weight and his legs crossed to give him some kind of dignity, while Sokka and Toph sat on the end of the mattress, Katara sat stiffly in the chair, and Aang was sitting on the bedside table, one foot dangling off, with the lemur perched on his head. This could only have been made more strange if Azula was somehow there, leaning on a wall acting like nothing had ever happened between them.

At some point, *someone* was going to have to break the silence. Explain why the Avatar was now sporting a shadow of dark hair on the top of his head, or *why* the other four had been so eager to just… eat *near* him. Everytime Zuko managed to catch Sokka’s eyes though, he shrugged or seemed flushed and would look away.

“This is awkward,” Toph said.

“*What*?” Aang said loudly, suddenly enough for Momo to hiss in annoyance, “It’s not… *awkward*,” he gave them a strange, pained smile, “it’s *fine*.”

“No,” Sokka said, shrugging, “Toph’s right.”

“Awkward.” Toph nodded.

Katara snapped her spoon against the bowl on her lap. “It was *your* idea,” she said angrily, to Toph, who seemed entirely unbothered.

“It’s *not* weird,” Aang insisted, “definitely not. Don’t you think so, Zuko?”

Zuko frowned at him. “I don’t know,” he reminded, “I’ve never had a meal with all of you before.”

“Sheesh,” Toph tapped her foot on the ground, “it’s not *me*. It’s all of *you* who are making things awkward.”

“What else did you *expect*?” Katara demanded. She glared around the room, looking at Sokka in particular, “Are we just supposed to act like we’re best friends all of the sudden? Like he isn’t *Fire* *Nation*?”

“You didn’t have any problem with the old guy,” Toph pointed out.

“*He’s* not *Zuko* ,” Katara said angrily. She sat back on her chair with a huff. “What else did you expect?”

Zuko couldn’t help but agree with her. *This*, the five of them sitting almost amicably in a room eating dinner, being allies, him in a room with the Avatar, Sokka dressed like a *Fire Nation soldier* - no. “It’s all unexpected,” he said.

“Hey, some common ground,” Sokka pointed out, jumping in, “Katara thinks it’s weird, you think it’s weird…” he gestured between the two of them, “eh?”

“What?” Katara said, deadpan and glaring.

“Why are you so quiet twinkletoes?” Toph asked, jumping in. She was pointing, raising an accusing finger at Aang, so Zuko guessed that was the person the name belonged to. “You were the one who couldn’t stop asking Katara how he was doing, *well*, he’s up? Now what?”

It was strange to think about how much time *had* passed, apparently. Where for Zuko nearly two weeks had ached on and yet quickly faded from memory, everyone else had been moving forward. While he’d just been here, waiting to wake up, and these other people he knew had been… *concerned*. About him.

Aang was perched up on table at Zuko’s left, and when Zuko looked at him he looked suddenly worried. “I…” he said, his eyes widening.

“Aang?” Sokka asked.

“I have to-" Aang suddenly jumped to his feet. He looked, wildly, between the group and announced, “I should check on Appa!”

“Aang,” Sokka started to say, “you don’t-"

Aang took three huge steps forward and, with a speed so fast he created a burst of wind in the room strong enough that Zuko had to close his eyes, ran out the door at an incredible speed. Gone in a second. Zuko blinked, staring at the space Aang had been a moment before.

“*Sokka*!” Katara said, jumping to her feet. She had her bowl in one hand, the spoon in the other like a weapon.

“What?” Sokka raised both his hands, his food balanced between his knees, “What did I do?”

“You are both just *so*-" Katara walked around the table, snatching up Aang’s food from Momo and whipping around to glare at them all, “*insensitive*.”

“Or,” Toph pointed out with a mouthful of food, “everyone else is *too* sensitive.”

Katara stared at Toph and Sokka, who both looked unbothered, Toph moreso, and then walked out of the room, muttering something under her breath that Zuko couldn’t hear clearly enough to understand.

Then it was just the three of them and the lemur. Zuko, sitting awkwardly propped up on a bed, Sokka staring at the bowl of food in his lap, and Toph, leaning backward, continuing to stuff her mouth with food as if nothing unusual happened.

“That’s uh,” Sokka said, raising his head to look at the door and wince, “Aang’s been a bit on edge.”

“And *Sweetness* is *always* on edge,” Toph said with a shrug.

“Okay.” Zuko nodded. *Okay*. He looked around the room, which was bare of anything that he could use to talk about beside a Fire Nation flag and an annoyed lemur. “I didn’t… ask,” he said, awkwardly, “*why* are you wearing that armor?”

Sokka raised a hand to the back of his neck. “Ah, well, we’re… everyone above deck has been in disguise just to be safe. After we left Ba Sing Se we made our way to the Water Tribe warriors, and they had captured this ship with Katara. So, we can use it to lay low as we make our way west. And before this I was, well…” he trailed off.

“Above deck?” Zuko asked him.

“Uh, yeah,” Sokka said, swallowing and lowering his hand. “So.”

“So.”

“Wow,” Toph said loudly, “you two are even *more* awkward.”

Zuko felt heat rising heavily on his face and he wished it *wouldn’t*. Even if she couldn’t see him blush, *Sokka* still could.

“We, we’re not-" Sokka sputtered at her.

“With how mopey *you* were I thought you’d both be like,” Toph smirked, “‘oh, *Zuko*, I missed you so much! *Mwah*, kiss kiss, I love you, ah’.”

Zuko blinked.

“*Toph*!”

“*Sokka*,” Toph said, chuckling. She stood up, putting her bowl on the bed, and for a moment Zuko thought she was also getting up to leave. Then she took a step forward, grabbed Zuko’s arm, and said in a strange high-pitched voice, “*Zuko*, I *love* you!”

Zuko tried to pull his arm away from her. “What are you *doing*?!” He snapped.

“*My prince*!” Toph exclaimed, putting her free hand on her forehead like she was about to faint, “Oh, my darling!”

Sokka jumped to his feet. “*Toph*,” he said, his voice cracking.

“What?” Toph asked him.

Zuko managed to shove her off of his arm. She just grinned at him.

“You should hear his heartbeat,” Toph said to Zuko, “it’s *so* fast.”

“Okay,” Zuko said.

“Toph!”

“What?” Toph asked, crossing her arms and frowning. Even standing beside the bed, she was almost shorter than Zuko and it was odd, realizing that an outrageous personality existed in such a small frame. “You’re shy?”

Sokka’s jaw dropped as he looked at her for a moment. “I am… *not* shy,” he said firmly, his eyes flickering to Zuko, “I am a warrior.”

“You’re acting like a shy little *girl*,” Toph told him, sticking out her tongue.

“*You’re* a little girl,” Zuko reminded her. She shrugged.

“You-" Sokka clenched his fists at his side. “I am a manly- *Toph*, c’mon.”

Toph chuckled by Zuko’s ear. “Manly?” She challenged, “How can you be manly when you have a *boyfriend*?”

Zuko glared at her.

"He's a *boy*friend,” Sokka said loudly, “two *boys*. It’s *twice* as manly!”

“Huh,” Toph brought a finger to her chin, enunciating each syllable thoughtfully, “I see your point.”

“Okay,” Sokka said, clearly bristling with anger. He walked around the bed, grabbing Toph’s bowl and shoving it toward her hands. “*Out*. Everyone leaves now. Take Momo.”

“*Hey*!”

Sokka took a handful of her shirt and pushed her toward the door. Toph laughed, but moved where he was guiding her. “Out, everyone is out, embarrassing Sokka hour is *over*,” he said.

“Aw,” Toph reached the door and took a step into the hallway. Then turned back with a wicked smirk on her face. “But *Sokka*, aren’t you going to show Zuko that drawing you did? The one Katara thought was a walrus-seal!”

Sokka seemed to freeze at the door, one hand holding it open. “Uh…”

“What drawing?” Zuko asked curiously.

Sokka shook his head. Then he swung the door shut, leaving Toph out in the hallway.

“You know,” Toph yelled from the other side, “I have to tell Zuko about the time you got stuck in a hole!”

“Go *away*!”

“It’s vital information!”

“It *never* happened!”

“This door is metal, you can’t *actually* keep me out, you know!”

Sokka slapped his forehead. “*Toph*, please,” he muttered.

“Alright, alright,” her voice sounded more distant now, like she was walking away but not before calling out, “I’m only leaving because *I* chose to!”

Sokka sighed, as if he’d just run a marathon or done something physically taxing, and leaned forward to press his forehead against the closed metal door.

Zuko looked at the back of Sokka’s head with interest. “You draw?”

Sokka stiffened. He turned around, the loose armor clicking against the door as he did. “Uh… sometimes?”

This seemed like a much better topic than Fire Navy uniform regulations or whatever was wrong with the Avatar. Zuko sat up more on the bed, holding back a grimace as pain twinged through his stomach, but it was fine. Dignified… almost. “What do you draw?” Zuko asked.

Sokka coughed. “Um… *stuff*,” he said.

“Stuff,” Zuko repeated blandly.

“Like uh,” Sokka walked forward, picking up his own bowl and setting it on the bedside table. Zuko did the same, able to reach it from where he was. Then, biting his lip as if he was nervous, Sokka sat down on the bed right by Zuko’s crossed knee. “Appa, and uh, Aang. The group, once. Mostly Appa,” he said, “you.”

“Why draw me?”

“Why… not?” Sokka asked him, seeming surprised Zuko even questioned it.

He was sitting near enough that Zuko’s knee was touching his leg; Zuko could see his brilliant blue eyes and that light dusting of freckles across his nose. Something in Zuko’s stomach tightened, which sent a small bit of pain across his stomach, enough to grimace.

“Sorry,” Sokka said immediately, eyes widening. “Do you not like getting drawn? It doesn’t even look like you, I’m not actually good at art I just… like it. I mean, I just started, so.”

“You’re good,” Zuko assured him, “I’m sure you’re good.”

“At drawing?” Sokka asked, frowning.

“Yes.”

Sokka snorted. “You haven’t even *seen* anything I’ve drawn.”

“Well, no,” Zuko admitted, “but you’re… good at a lot of things.”

“Doesn’t mean I’m good at *art*,” Sokka said, chuckling, apparently to himself. He looked down at his hands. “Uh, it was just sort of, something to do. While I was watching you sleeping.”

Zuko swallowed. “You…” he said slowly, heat rising in his face, “*watched* me sleep?”

Sokka’s head surged upward. “Not, I mean-“ his voice cracked, “not like, in a *weird* - I just- I was… I mean, I also played some game with your uncle or- I wasn’t,” he seemed panicked, “*always*, watching you- it was more, just…”

“No, it’s…” Zuko made himself cough. He wished he could banish the blush off his face with sheer force of will. “Fine.”

“I was just… I mean your uncle watched you *too*,” Sokka told him, “we both- so it, was, I wasn’t- I mean I did watch you *a lot* but-"

“A lot?” Zuko interrupted. Had he talked in his sleep? Had he, what had he *looked* like- with the fever, and just *lying* there?

“It was,” Sokka said. Paused. “I was just…” He winced, his expression dropping, “if you woke up, I wanted to be in the room, but I wasn’t, and really it was more about if you… *didn’t*. Wake up.” Zuko stared at him. One of his hands was on his stomach, right over the injury as he puzzled over Sokka’s face; he seemed to very quickly be getting more and more upset as Zuko didn’t know what to say. “I *am* awake,” Zuko pointed out eventually.

“*Yes*,” Sokka breathed, “you’re awake.” Sokka was looking at him, in a way Zuko really didn’t know how to describe. With eyes that were wide, shining and wet, but wide-eyed and so entirely *focused*. It was nice and at the same time so supremely uncomfortable that Zuko almost wanted to shove Sokka off the bed to stop it.

“Yes,” Zuko said slowly.

“And alive,” Sokka reminded him, his voice suddenly very quiet.

“Yes,” Zuko said again.

Sokka nodded at him slowly. “You almost… you know you,” one of his hands reached out to grab the pelt blanket by Zuko’s leg. His hand was shaking. “Almost died.”

“I didn’t,” Zuko said. Keeping his hand on his stomach, which was starting to throb, he leaned forward as much as he could. “I’m fine, trust me, it’s not…” he wasn’t sure what to do. If this was Iroh it would have been easier, he would have understood what to… say, or do, but this was *Sokka* . He couldn’t do this *wrong*. This was new. Uncertain. Zuko didn’t know the rules yet. “It’s not the first time I nearly died,” Zuko offered, forcing himself to smile in a way he hoped was reassuring, “or even the third, really.”

“Oh?” Sokka whispered.

“Yeah,” Zuko shrugged. He put his other hand on the bed, close enough to Sokka’s to be nearly touching. “When I was born my father thought I wasn’t a bender, he nearly cast me from the palace. And when I was *ten* my grandfather was… stuff happened. And when I lost my- when my face was burned, the ship doctor apparently thought I wouldn’t pull through,” Zuko told him. “I might be too stubborn to die.”

When he looked up from their hands to meet Sokka’s face again, Sokka’s eyes were wet. His jaw was trembling and there was water building up along his lashes and his face was crumbling and Zuko felt something jolt in his chest - panic. It was panic. “I,” Zuko said frantically, “I mean, this… are you…” *Shit*. If he pointed it out Sokka could be embarrassed, if he *didn’t* would that make it seem like he didn’t care?

“‘m, hm,” Sokka said, nodding slowly. “Okay.”

“So,” Zuko started to say, and wasn’t sure what else to say after. He willed himself to *think*. Do *something*.

Sokka acted first. One moment his hands were down and the next they surged forward, grabbing Zuko’s shoulders, and then he was pulling Zuko forward into an urgent hug. One of the shoulders of Sokka’s armor conked against Zuko’s chin and Zuko said, “Ow!” before he could stop himself.

Abruptly, Sokka pulled away. He had a horrified expression on his face. “I’m sorry,” he said, looking down at Zuko’s stomach, “did I hurt-"

“No!” Zuko promised, “No, that’s fine. *I’m* fine.”

“I shouldn’t have done that, you’re injured-"

“No it- just the *armor*,” Zuko told him.

Sokka blinked at him for moment, then his eyes widened. “Oh-" he dropped his hand to the straps on his shoulder, rapid hands fumbling at clasps that were loose enough to make it more difficult to grap, “this stupid armor, how’d you wear it all the time- I *wish* you’d kept wearing it probably wouldn’t have-"

“You get used to it,” Zuko said absentmindedly, frowning as he watched Sokka undoing the armor with shaking hands. “If you get your hands under the,” he said, moving to the fastenings on Sokka’s waist and undoing them with unpracticed but familiar motions, “here, it can just lift off.”

“Right, I forgot,” Sokka said quickly, his voice cracking. After a few more moments of clumsy motions he succeeded, lifting the armor off of his head and dropping it to the ground beside them with a clank loud enough that they both winced. He was just wearing russet leathers then, which were much too loose on his arms and shoulders, and it was… very strange. To see Sokka in *red*. Zuko didn’t have much time to focus on that though, before Sokka was wrapping his arms around Zuko’s neck and holding him tight.

Sokka held himself against Zuko’s side, the hardest part of his grip on Zuko’s shoulders and neck. His face under Zuko’s neck and chin like he’d been hurled forward, or was being careful about putting too much pressure on Zuko and at the same time wanting to squeeze the breath out of him. His wolftail tickled the underside of Zuko’s nose, he was warm, he smelled like the salty sea air, *oh*, it was *nice*.

Zuko wrapped his arms around Sokka too, grabbing that leather shirt tight in his hands and pulling him just a bit closer. *Not just nice,* Zuko thought, as Sokka held him back like he also didn’t want to let go, *lovely*.

“You’re really warm,” Sokka mumbled, and Zuko could feel the words exhaled on his neck.

Perfect, it was perfect. He dropped his head to press his nose into Sokka’s hair, mouth touching the shorn side of his head that seemed a bit longer than Zuko remembered. Sokka’s back shook, jolting up slightly. Zuko didn’t think much of it, just holding him tighter, until it happened again, then again, with a hitching breath and he realized Sokka was crying.

“I’m so,” Sokka seemed to be straining to talk, “*glad* you didn’t- just the *worst.* ”

What would Iroh do? Besides hold him, which Zuko was *already doing*. Something deep in his chest ached.

“I said,” Sokka’s arms loosened slightly, “she *died*. The first person I kissed. And when you nearly, when your hand was covered in blood and then… you were *fading* and you started talking to the air… I just…” Zuko grabbed Sokka tighter, not knowing what else to do. One hand stayed on his back, the other gripped the side of Sokka’s head and ear and pulled him close as Zuko pressed his face hard enough against the side of Sokka’s neck that his nose hurt. “I’m not- not upset, I’m *happy*, really, it’s so stupid- thank you.” Sokka’s voice was *rough* , and Zuko hated the sound of it like this. “Thank you, for not dying, that sounds so weird-"

“It’s fine,” Zuko promised. He lifted his head, just enough to look at Sokka’s, shaking pressed against him and Zuko grimaced. Wished he could make him stop. Make him *feel better.* It should feel nice, to have someone crying over *him,* that’s what Zuko thought he’d wanted before, but when his uncle had cried all Zuko had wanted was for it to *end* and Zuko felt the same way now. “You have feelings,” Zuko started to say, then paused, mind racing as he tried to figure out where he was going with that.

By some stroke of luck, Sokka chuckled. “*Everyone* has feelings,” he said.

“I just care about yours right now,” Zuko said sincerely.

Sokka sat up, sniffing. His eyes were suddenly swollen, his face looked heavy as he raised his head enough to meet Zuko’s. He wiped a hand under her nose. Sokka looked miserable.

Zuko lifted both his hands to Sokka’s cheeks, staring at him, willing himself to think of *anything* to say to fix this.

“I,” Sokka said, swallowing, “I care about your feelings too. Even if you *are* a jerk.”

Sokka smiled. He *smiled*, his lips curling upward near Zuko’s palms as he met Zuko’s gaze, warm blue eyes staring back. Zuko blinked at him for a moment, waiting for something else to happen, or Sokka to cry again, as Zuko’s stomach lurched; but Sokka’s smile just seemed to get wider the longer he looked at Zuko.

---

This wasn’t the bright green field behind the library, it was a metal box with poor light sources, unsteadily squealing and rolling with larger ocean waves, it was a bed covered in haphazard fur blankets that was a far cry from a lush green clearing tucked between trees, but it felt the same, somehow. Maybe just because they were both there, lying next to each other, Zuko on his back and Sokka rolled over on his side.

Sokka must have felt the similarities too, because after a long, quiet moment of just looking at Zuko, he reached a finger out to tap Zuko’s shoulder and said, “This is better when you aren’t wearing a mask.”

Zuko looked back at him, Sokka on his right, and frowned. “It is?”

“Definitely,” Sokka said, pulling his hand back to lean his arm against it. His head over Zuko’s shoulder now, looking down at him. “Why wouldn’t it be?”

“I…” *my face*, “that’s obvious, isn’t it?”

“What’s obvious?” Sokka raised an eyebrow.

“I would think,” Zuko said slowly, “of the two of us, you… have the better view. All things considered.”

Sokka looked curious for a moment, blinking down at Zuko with his mouth in a tight line before his eyes brightened. Then he shrugged. “Hey,” Sokka said, “don’t insult my view. I happened to *like* my view.”

“Oh.” Zuko dropped his gaze, looking at Sokka’s hands, the left tucked behind his head and the other resting by the other arm’s elbow. He lifted his own hand, just close enough to brush along soft brown knuckles, feeling like he was musing on something, ruminating in thought, when there was nothing in his head but emptiness.

This was peaceful. There wasn’t… Zuko wasn’t thinking about a way for this to *end*. It *wouldn’t* end, not if he didn’t want it to, they could stay like this, doing nothing, until the sun dropped low. Until it rose again, even, and plan to sit together on another day. It didn’t need to end.

“Are you okay?” Sokka asked him in a quiet voice.

“*Yes*,” Zuko said earnestly. He raised his head, to look at wide, blue eyes framed with a kind expression, and something gentle and warm filled his chest. “I’m very okay.”

“Well,” Sokka shifted a bit, just to get more comfortable it seemed, “*besides* that whole ‘healing from a stab wound’ thing?” He moved his hand, turning it enough that their fingers met. “And whatever your uncle was on about weird Fire Nation laws, I guess.”

“No idea what he was talking about,” Zuko lied.

Sokka raised an eyebrow and grinned. “*Sure*.” He moved again, lifting himself up until they were even closer, close enough now that Zuko could fill his vision with nothing but Sokka’s face. “So. What is on your mind, right now? What does *Prince Zuko* think about when he does nothing with me?”

Zuko thought for a moment. “Nothing,” he said truthfully, but corrected himself, “or a lot of things. It just… depends.”

“I, Sokka, wonder,” Sokka asked him, “if you know how *nice* it is, looking in your eyes.”

Zuko blinked at him, something in Sokka’s cadence hitting a note in his mind.

“Like a sunset gold,” Sokka mused, his fingers twining around Zuko’s, “or golden-“

“Was that a haiku?” Zuko interrupted when the thought finally connected.

Sokka froze. “Uh,” he looked down for a moment, then flickered his eyes back and said sheepishly, “yes.”

“Poetry?” Zuko asked.

“Well, haiku’s *are* poetry so, yes. Do you…” Sokka asked, seeming uneasy, “like poetry?”

“I do *now*,” Zuko said eagerly. He sat up a bit on his elbows, moving even closer to Sokka. “Say it again.”

“Is that an *order*?” Sokka asked him with a grin. “There are actually more stanzas.”

“Really?” Zuko asked him, his heart pounding a rhythm not unlike jumping off a tall building but so welcome, so *bright*.

“Yeah,” Sokka said, his nose and cheeks flushing darker. “Hm, so, like a sunset gold-"

Zuko didn’t hear any of the rest. He’d reached out for Sokka’s neck, pulled him closer, and was kissing him before Sokka could say another word.

---

“‘m, *poetry*. Is there anything you aren’t good at?”

“Ha! You’re serious?”

“Definitely.”

“Well… I haven’t beaten your uncle at pai sho yet, but I did only *just* learn how to play.”

“You will.”

“Thanks but, you can stop talking.”

“Ah, *alright*.”

---

“Your hair grows out fast,” Sokka pointed out, as if it had just occurred to him despite having been running his hands through Zuko’s hair for so long Zuko couldn’t hope to guess. His right leg was thrown over Zuko’s waist, casual, meanwhile his arms were one over and one under Zuko’s, hands holding his head and lifting Zuko slightly up from the bed.

For his part, Zuko had one hand on Sokka’s knee and the other low on his back, his nose against Sokka’s and his mouth breathing hotly into Sokka’s ear. Which Sokka seemed to enjoy quite a lot. Zuko muttered a response, something, not even sure if it was words.

Zuko had experienced a lot of strange and new things since he’d come to Ba Sing Se. He’d been drunk, he’d taken a strange spirit drug the nature of which he wasn't even sure of, and yet he hadn’t realized anyone could feel *this* high from *touch* . From *holding* and being held back. Tangled up as much as he could against Sokka’s boney frame, he was certain he probably had bruises from Sokka’s elbows somewhere but Zuko wasn’t bothered, the opposite, it was proof he was *there*. He’d made the right choice. *Sokka liked him*.

“Hum, *so*,” Sokka said, his hands sliding along Zuko’s hair like he was petting an animal. It was *nice* , though. He didn’t want Sokka to *stop* brushing his hair.

Zuko turned his head just slightly, still pushed into Sokka’s. “‘n?” Zuko asked, pursing his lips just enough into Sokka’s to technically be a kiss, even if his mouth had never left in the first place.

“How long,” Sokka said, chuckling a bit, “do you think it’ll take before someone decides to check- "

There were three loud knocks on the door.

“-on us,” Sokka concluded sourly.

Zuko lifted his head up slowly to look at the door, his lip curling.

“Speak of a spirit,” Sokka muttered, which sounded like the start of a proverb. He dropped his hands from Zuko’s head to the mattress, lifting himself up with a groan.

“I’ll make them go,” Zuko decided. He sat up, one hand immediately grabbing his stomach which twinged with pain in response. Zuko had barely done anything in nearly two weeks besides sleep but his body apparently found just walking to a bathroom and lying down with Sokka enough effort that it wanted to protest. He felt a bit like a kid again, clumsy and weak with a body that refused to do what he wanted.

Sokka had moved onto his knees, patting his palms onto the mattress like he was looking for something. His loose hair was curled down by his mouth now, framing his face, one strand dropping near his nose as he lifted his head to look at Zuko. “Huh?”

Steeling himself, determined not to give away that he was hurting, Zuko forced himself to stand in one solid motion. It was fine, besides some blood rushing quickly enough to his head to force him to blink and refocus his sight. After that, he stepped aside the armor lying on the floor and rounded the bed, smooth long paces, before he reached the door to the room.

Glaring, Zuko flung open the door and growled, “*What*?!”

Iroh stood in the doorway, unimpressed. He raised an eyebrow at Zuko, then leaned over to look past his shoulder at Sokka. “Hello, young man,” Iroh said pleasantly.

“Hel- your *uncle*! Hello!” From behind Zuko’s back, he heard something heavy fall to the ground, a conk that sounded as if Sokka had knocked his feet straight into the armor left on the ground and a loud, “*Ow*.”

Zuko kept his eyes on his uncle, hand still on the door. “What is it?” Zuko demanded.

Iroh had a smile on his face that was half a degree from a smirk as he met Zuko’s gaze with knowing eyes. “It’s getting a little late,” he said, “I think it’s time your guest left and let you rest.”

Zuko frowned.

“Ah, it’s late?” Sokka asked.

“Yes, young man,” Iroh said happily, “I’m sure you two can continue catching up tomorrow.”

“Right, right, *where are my shoes*,” Sokka was saying behind him, something metal clicking as he moved around.

“That alright, nephew?” Iroh’s eyes flickered to Zuko’s arm blocking the door and then his gaze went back to Zuko’s face.

His teeth gritted tight, Zuko forced himself to answer, “*Fine*.”

Iroh chuckled at him, and Zuko felt a vein on his forehead twitching in annoyance. A moment later though, Sokka bounded up to Zuko’s side, his hair still down on his face, holding the armor and his shoes in a large bundle in front of his chest. His shoulders tensing, Zuko lowered his hand from the door and took a step back.

“See you tomorrow,” Sokka said, his voice high pitched like he was nervous, “Zuko, and uh-*Uncle*.”

“I’ll… see you,” Zuko said quietly.

Sokka grinned, awkwardly walking through the door sideways to avoid the both of them. He took two steps down the hall, before stopping to look at Zuko again.

Iroh gave Sokka a wave, stepped into the room, and shut the door.

“Alright,” his uncle said, taking Zuko’s elbow in one hand and guiding him back to the bed while Zuko glared. “I meant it. You need your rest.”

“I’m *going*,” Zuko said with annoyance. He pulled Iroh’s hand off of him and took an embarrassingly difficult few steps back to the bed. He sat down with a groan, his hand on his stomach tensing.

As Iroh glanced around the room, stepping over to the table to look at the two bowls of food as Zuko swung his legs back onto the bed. “You didn’t eat much,” Iroh mused, one hand on his chin, “what *were* you two doing? Hm?”

Zuko swallowed to keep the heat from rising on his face and declined to answer.

His uncle took the bowl and walked over to the chair, sitting down and handing it to Zuko without a word.

He *was*, in fact, hungry. Now that Zuko actually took a moment to think about it. He kept his eyes on the food, heating the bottom of the bowl as he spun the spoon through the jook. They were quiet for a while. Zuko was grateful for that. His uncle seemed lost in thought while Zuko was content to just sit and eat.

Iroh was right about it being late, now that Zuko was paying attention he could feel the sun lowering down somewhere by the horizon, his inner fire waning in response. He *was* tired.

Zuko had just brought the first bite to his mouth when Iroh broke the silence saying, “You are very much like I was at your age.”

It took every bit of Zuko’s strength not to spit his food out. He swallowed, throat scratching, coughing, and stared at his uncle.

“I was *quite* the charmer in my day,” Iroh told Zuko with a bright smile, “ah, the girls would swoon after me.”

Zuko kept coughing, looking at Iroh in disbelief.

“Now look at *you*,” Iroh chuckled, reaching out to nudge Zuko in the arm, “with these fetching boys, eh?”

Barely managing to still his cough, Zuko glared at his uncle.

“It’s our good looks,” Iroh continued, as if entirely unaware of Zuko’s aggravation, “*ah*, young romance. Those were the days.”

“*What*,” Zuko hissed at him, “do you *want*?”

“I think now is the time you and I have a *different* kind of serious talk,” Iroh told Zuko.

“No.”

His uncle patted Zuko’s arm comfortingly. “I’m afraid there’s no getting out of this one.”

---

Katara and Sokka came by early in the morning for another round of healing, this time Sokka was dressed in his blue Water Tribe clothing. She was stiff, but made some small talk, glancing over the entire time at Sokka who was hovered nearby doing nothing. As she left, Katara asked Zuko to talk to Aang.

Zuko *planned* to, of course, but Katara came back three hours later to find him and Sokka sitting on the bed in an animated discussion about sailing passages between the Fire Nation islands, a map Sokka had brought spread out on the mattress in front of them, and with an angry look on her face as she demanded to know if Zuko had talked to Aang yet. Sokka grumbled at her, promising they would find him soon.

Two hours after that she stopped by *again* to find them in the exact same place, this time curled around each other while Sokka was telling Zuko about tracking techniques along ice terrains and the time he’d been following what he thought was a walrus-seal for four hours until he realized it was just a penguin and his own footprints going around in circles. *That* time Katara had shouted, and Sokka had reluctantly promised, “okay, *okay*, I *said* ‘okay’,” that they’d find Aang *now*.

Zuko really didn’t blame himself for forgetting. Sokka being distracting was just a fact.

When they finally were walking out into the ship Zuko realized this was actually the first time he’d stepped out of the room. First time he’d been inside these tight, familiar and yet unfamiliar metal corridors, with their torch riggings, tight corners, and the near claustrophobic nature of it all. It was almost soothing, easy, to be back in an environment he’d spent three years in, if it wasn’t for the men who passed by them.

Sokka greeted the first group, three of them, all in Fire Navy uniform despite clearly water tribe hairstyles. They were tall, broad shouldered, had names that washed over Zuko’s ears to immediately be forgotten in his current state, and looked at Zuko with intense suspicion. Sokka waved, introduced Zuko and continued. He was telling Zuko something about the difficulty the warriors had in adjusting their sailing techniques to this type of ship, not noticing as Zuko turned his head to look behind him.

Three warriors, standing still in the hall, watching Zuko walk away. One put his hand onto his hip, where a weapon was hitched. Zuko glared back, breathed a spark from his mouth with a snarl, and didn’t stop watching them until they’d turned the corner.

“If I know Aang he’ll be up top,” Sokka was saying. Ahead were the stairs to the surface, at the bottom of which was a pile of fabric. Zuko didn’t understand the point, until Sokka leaned down and picked up a cloak, pinning it over his clothing to conceal his blue uniform. “You’re fine,” Sokka told Zuko, looking at his clothing, “even if you’re not wearing armor? Right?”

Zuko glanced down at the red tunic and pants he was wearing, Fire Nation style down to his shoes. “I’ll pass for a chef,” he said with a shrug.

“Alright,” Sokka said with a smile, taking the first step up the stairs, “time to find- *oh*.” Sokka froze, one hand on the wall, the other suddenly tensing at his side.

Zuko frowned at him, then looked upward curiously at the person blocking the light.

The man didn’t seem as intimidating as some of the others, only a few inches taller than Zuko. He was wearing a cloak too, one thrown behind his shoulders to show Water Tribe clothing that didn’t seem different from anyone else’s besides a larger necklace of whittled teeth and bone. “Sokka,” he said. In a voice that, again, didn’t seem *that* intimidating, “I *did* ask to know when he was awake enough for guests.” The man looked at Zuko, a frown on his face, one eyebrow raised almost comically suspiciously up on his forehead.

“*Right*,” Sokka said loudly, “uh- *so…*”

“If you’re talking about *me*,” Zuko said with a scowl, “I’d prefer to be addressed correctly.”

“Zuko,” the man said, emphasizing the word to make it clear, even to Zuko, that he was making a point out of not saying his title, “I am Chief Hakoda.”

*Ah*, that would be where the intimidation came from on Sokka’s part. The leader of the warriors, and the south. “*Hakoda*, are you going to let us *pass*?” Zuko asked him, clenching his fists at his sides.

Sokka turned around sharply at Zuko, making some kind of expression but Zuko didn’t move his eyes to see. He met Hakoda’s gaze firmly, determined not to be the one who looked away first.

“We need to talk,” Hakoda told him sternly.

“*Why* would I do that?” Zuko asked, his breath hot, “I’m not about to *agree* to an interrogation.” “It might have escaped you while you’d been sleeping,” Hakoda said stoically, ignoring Sokka waving a hand between the two of them, “but this is my ship you’re standing in.”

“It looks Fire Nation to me.”

Hakoda narrowed his eyes. “Is that how we’re-"

“Hey!” Sokka jumped between the two of them, breaking their line of sight. He reached out, grabbed Zuko’s hand before Zuko could say a word of protest, and, gesticulating wildly between them, “Zuko, *my father*, my father, this is Zuko. Wow! So great you’ve met. We have to go see Aang, so, talk later! Bye.”

Sokka *yanked*, with enough force that Zuko stumbled forward, and pulled him by the hand up the stairs. Hakoda, still staring at Zuko with mistrustful eyes, stepped aside while they passed. Zuko glared right back.

They made it up the rest of the stairs, out onto the deck into a late afternoon sun. There were a handful of other warriors up on deck, dressed in full Fire Navy armor, the only one who wasn’t appeared to be washing some clothing up by the mast. The water surged around them, loud, splashing, the air suddenly much more salty than metallic. An ocean at ease with a firm but quiet continuous wind bustling over the weather deck.

Zuko didn’t get much of a chance to observe, or to look at these other warriors, as Sokka nearly dragged him away from the others. Someone laughed, another person made a joke. Sokka didn’t seem to care, just pulled them both away from the head of the ship to the back.

No one seemed to be working here, though they wouldn’t be alone. Zuko glanced upward, toward the stacks billowing out their smoke and the upper navigator’s deck, spotting an orange figure sitting on the main mast, right above the Fire Nation flag. *Aang*, Zuko recognized.

Sokka dropped Zuko’s hand when they were completely in the shade at the back of the ship, whipping around to face Zuko with his hands clenched by his face. He seemed… mad, confused, annoyed, Sokka was making *a lot* of faces at him. All of which cumulated in Sokka just yelling, “*What*?!”

Zuko looked at him carefully. He took in Sokka’s wide eyes, twitching hands, eyebrows raised high on his head, open mouth, and… Zuko just wasn’t *sure* exactly what all of it was supposed to mean. “What?” Zuko asked back.

“‘*What*’?” Sokka repeated, his voice getting higher with each word, “What do you mean *what*?”

Zuko frowned at him. Then shrugged. He pointed upward, “I can see Aang on the flag-"

“Forget about Aang for a second!” Sokka dropped both his hands onto Zuko’s shoulders. “*Zuko*,” he said seriously.

“Sokka?”

“I just,” Sokka pulled one hand back to pinch his nose, “that was my *dad*.”

“I know,” Zuko pointed out, “you introduced us.”

Sokka closed his eyes. “Of course this wouldn’t be easy.”

“I don’t owe *him* anything,” Zuko told Sokka angrily, “I saved the Avatar’s life, I betrayed my own family to be here, if he thinks I’ll just sit down and recognize *his* authority-"

“You can’t?” Sokka asked Zuko.

“I’m not going to just *let* someone interrogate me!”

“*Okay*!” Sokka dropped his hand from his face, opening his eyes and looking extremely aggravated, “But you could at least *be nice*.”

“Why?” Zuko asked him, confused. “You’re the one who didn’t want to see him, and you said he left you for years- you aren’t even that close.”

“I *know*,” Sokka said, grimacing.

“So, why does it matter?”

“Because I, because I’d *like to be,* ” Sokka sighed. He dropped his hand from Zuko’s shoulder to cross his arms in front of his chest. “I would *like* to be close. With my father. And I, *ugh*,” he groaned, “And I might have made the worst impression *ever* with him, considering I haven’t seen him in years and then it’s like- guess what! I have a boyfriend, and he’s *Prince Zuko*.” Sokka raised an eyebrow at Zuko and leaned forward. “That was *not* an easy conversation.”

Oh. “I can see how that wouldn’t have been easy,” Zuko acknowledged.

“*Right*,” Sokka said, looking Zuko straight in the eyes. “I think it’d be a lot better for the both of us, you know, while we are *on this ship* with them, if everyone got along,” he said, “I don’t want my father to hate you.”

Zuko nodded but his fists tightened at his sides. “If you think the opinion of our fathers is supposed to matter,” Zuko pointed out stiffly, “you may have forgotten who mine is.”

“Hm,” Sokka seemed thoughtful. Then he leaned forward even closer, a grin on his face, and said in a strangely sweet voice, “You can’t be nice to him for me?”

Zuko felt something anxious in his stomach. “Of course I can,” he promised, “I just-"

“Cmon,” Sokka encouraged, “just, be nice to him for me?” And then, enunciating each syllable heavily, “Your turtle*duck*?”

Instant, flushing heat snapped into Zuko’s face. “I…”

“Will you?” Sokka took a step even closer, “My little-"

“*Don’t*,” Zuko whispered.

Sokka looked at Zuko’s face and then burst out laughing. A laugh that almost immediately turned into a pained wheeze.

“*Sokka*,” Zuko frowned at him.

“Oh, c’mon,” Sokka said through his fits of laughter, clutching a hand onto his stomach, “you should *see* your face, you just-"

Zuko grabbed Sokka’s shoulder, turning his own body and pushing to force him to back up against the nearby wall. He made a startled noise, as Zuko stepped closer into his space and- something in Zuko’s stomach *twisted*, a painful twitch that had him doubling over.

“Whoa,” Sokka’s hands were immediately around him, helping Zuko to stay standing.

“‘m fine,” Zuko said, at the same time doing his best not to fall over.

“Got it, got it,” Sokka said, and at the same time holding Zuko up carefully. He turned around and bent down, bringing Zuko with him, and slowly helped guide Zuko to sit. “You good?”

Zuko winced, aftershocks of the strain on his body still coursing through his stomach, but it was much easier. “Yes,” Zuko said, taking in a deep steadying breath, “I’m-"

“My turtleduck?” Sokka said, nonchalantly.

Zuko lifted his gaze to glare at him. “*Sokka*.”

“Now,” Sokka said with a smirk, kneeling over him, “what happened to turtleduck?” He looked at Zuko for a moment and then laughed, “You are *so* mad.”

“Yes,” Zuko said with a sneer.

Then, as if it was a completely ordinary thing to do, Sokka leaned forward and pressed his lips to Zuko’s nose.

*Alright*, that… that was nice. As a good amount of the tension in his shoulders and chest faded, instantly, as if by magic, and along with that went a good amount of the pain, Zuko realized with horror that if Sokka insisted on calling him that name, Zuko *was* *going to let him.* He’d probably let Sokka call him anything he wanted, which was a frightening amount of his dignity Zuko was willing to put on the line.

It was worth it, as Sokka pulled away with a bright grin, his head still close, bright, brilliant blue eyes blinking at Zuko’s, a deeper and more fascinating color than even the sky, because inside of them was some twinkling humor and a kind look, a *happy* gaze, meant for Zuko. “You have to talk to Aang,” Sokka said quietly, his expression growing soft.

“I will,” Zuko told him.

“Yeah,” Sokka said, shifting his weight on his knees and leaning closer. “We have a lot to do.”

“Play nice,” Zuko muttered, unable to stop himself from looking at Sokka’s mouth, “talk to Aang, plan an invasion, defeat my father.”

“*Yeah*.”

“Should focus on that.” Zuko reached out blindly, managing to find Sokka’s forearm and trail his knuckles down until he found Sokka’s hand.

“*Yeah*?” Sokka’s nose touched Zuko’s cheek, “Turtleduck?”

Zuko pushed him off.

Sokka fell to his side with a huff, still holding Zuko’s hand as he dropped to the deck. It took only a second before he was laughing, his free hand on his mouth to try to hold it back. It took a significant amount of Zuko’s energy not to smile. “*Okay*,” Sokka chuckled, wiping at one of his eyes, “bad timing.”

“Yes,” Zuko confirmed, the corners of his mouth twitching. He *liked* this, for some reason, this kind of teasing, or being made fun of it… wasn’t malicious. It was fun. Playful. So very *Sokka*. “You,” Sokka pointed at Zuko, “talk to Aang. I’ll go find something to eat and run interference with my dad. *Then*, we’ll, you know, overthrow the Fire Lord, or whatever.”

“Or whatever,” Zuko repeated.

Sokka stood up, cracking his back, and didn’t seem to realize Zuko was still holding his hand until Zuko brought it to his mouth and kissed it. Sokka froze.

Zuko let go of his hand and Sokka, hiding a bright grin, coughed. “Aang!” He whipped around, walking out onto the deck, “Come on out, buddy!”

---

The Avatar, sitting next to Zuko, had his knees curled up to his chest and kept itching at his scalp.

Zuko worried a piece of skin in his mouth between his teeth. He was leaning against the metal wall, one leg outstretched with the other bent casually enough to rest his forearm on, taking up a lot more space than Aang seemed comfortable with. He could probably ask him why Aang wasn’t wearing a cloak to hide his Air Nomad clothing, or *why* he had a black stubble of hair on his head, considering one was an act of defiance and *not* hiding and the other clearly *was* an attempt to disguise himself.

Or, Zuko could mention the breeze. A gentle southern wind that swirled over the sides of the ship and above, cool and pleasant. Perhaps the sight of the sky darkening as the sun lowered in the horizon, or the clouds overhead where a nearly imperceptible air bison ducked in and out as the wind moved. Preferably, Zuko could demand Aang get right down to it and *tell him* what he wanted to say. A strong part of Zuko would have preferred that, to grab the airbender by the shirt and order him to get *whatever this was* over with; clearly that wasn’t an *option* anymore. It wasn’t like before. When Zuko was hunting him. Stalking his every move to capture the Avatar and bring him back to his father. This was *now*. Where Zuko was, against all odds, *on Aang’s side* and had redirected lightning toward his own sister and her forces to save him.

Zuko sighed. He should-

“I’m sorry,” Aang said suddenly.

*Of course* he was the first one to break the silence. Zuko grimaced. Aang extending an olive branch to Zuko, *again*.

“I wanted to talk to you,” Aang said into his knees, “I should have asked myself, and- I know you and Sokka probably want to spend more time together.”

Aang wasn’t wrong, but considering Sokka had just asked Zuko to be nice Zuko bit back that response and just said, “Okay.”

Aang wrapped his arms around his legs, drawing his knees even closer to his chest. “I wish I was in love,” he said sadly.

“What.” Zuko blinked at him.

“Because you love each other,” Aang explained, making a face almost like he was pouting, “I bet it’s nice. Maybe I am in love, I don’t kn…”

“You’re just a *child*,” Zuko interrupted, scowling, “you have more important things to think about right now.”

Aang rested his chin on his knee and looked confused at Zuko. “*You’re* just a teenager with more important things to think about right now,” he said, as if he was making a point.

“I’m- *not*,” Zuko wasn’t *in love* , that meant, a *lot*, he liked Sokka, they were… boyfriends, Zuko guessed, considering Sokka had said that twice and Zuko wasn’t the slightest bit opposed, but he wasn’t- about to say- “Exactly. More important things to do.”

Aang sighed. “Love is beautiful,” he said, looking out into the sky.

“Stop saying that word!” Zuko demanded.

“Why?”

“Because we,” Zuko paled, “we just- we only… just *stop*! What did you want to talk about?”

Aang’s shoulders tensed. “Uh…”

“You want to talk to me,” Zuko said, his voice still clearly annoyed, “so what is it you want to say?”

“I…” Aang started.

“And *don’t*,” Zuko raised a finger, “say ‘love’ again.”

Aang looked down at his shoes. “No, that wasn’t what I wanted to talk to you about.”

“Fine.” Zuko frowned at him. Then he waited, for a long while, as Aang looked away from him and didn’t say anything. “Well?”

“I lost the Avatar State,” Aang said, his voice very quiet, “and when we were fighting, against Azula, and for Ba Sing Se, if I had it I might have been able to stop everything.”

Zuko shrugged. “Maybe,” he said, “but you couldn’t.”

“The thing is,” Aang said slowly, “I could have.”

Zuko tensed his hand at his side and looked away from him, over toward the edge of the ship. “You said you lost the Avatar State, so you couldn’t,” he gritted his teeth, “trust me, dwelling forever about what you *should have done* won’t do anything but make you miserable. It will only make it harder to do what you need to do.”

“Well,” Aang said softly, “there *was* a way I might have been able to access the Avatar State.”

“Then you should have,” Zuko said simply.

“But I would have lost… *something*. I didn’t want to.”

“Then it’s good you didn’t.”

“What?!” Aang stood up, throwing his arms in the air, “That’s the opposite of what you *just* *said*!”

Zuko glared at him. “So? Why are you talking to *me* about this anyway? There is a whole ship,” Zuko gestured around him, “of other people who would be far better at this.”

“*Because,* I-“ Aang’s eyes were wide, worried, “because I need to apologize.”

“Why? Who to?” Zuko asked.

“To you.”

“Me?” Zuko frowned up at him in disbelief, “Why would you apologize to *me*?”

Aang crossed his arms. “Because if I just accessed the Avatar State, you… would’ve been okay.”

“You *didn’t*, it’s over,” Zuko said sternly, “drop it.”

“I can’t,” Aang bit his lip and shook his head, “Ba Sing Se wouldn’t have been lost and you would be okay-"

“What happened *happened* . It’s done.” Zuko’s shoulders tensed and he sat up straighter, adding, “You can’t change the past. You have to move forward.”

“I’m s-"

“Don’t apologize to me or I’ll have to apologize to you and then we’ll be here until sunrise,” Zuko said bitterly. “I thought stopping Azula from killing you meant we wouldn’t have to do this.”

Aang looked at Zuko like he was trying to solve a puzzle. “I guess,” he said after a long pause, “if that’s what you want.”

“If it’s Avatar stuff you need help with,” Zuko offered, “ask my uncle. He knows a lot about the spirit world.”

“Okay.” Aang fidgeted. Then, after looking at Zuko and then the floor where Aang had just been sitting down on, he fidgeted some more before sitting back down. Aang crossed his legs in front of him, and sighed. “Alright.” Aang reached a hand up and scratched his head.

“What’s with the hair?” Zuko asked him.

Aang frowned, dropping his hand to his lap. “Well, your uncle helped the others find this safe passage through the Fire Nation blockade, around some of the islands, but everyone thinks Appa and I are too…”

“Obvious.” Zuko nodded.

“Yeah, and they’ll be looking for us. So, when we reach a drop off point, we’re going to split up. Go undercover through the Fire Nation away from the ship, and then meet back up later- but,” Aang frowned deeply. “I have to look… not like me.”

It made sense to Zuko, though he could see from Aang’s expression and slumped shoulders that he wasn't happy about it. He *knew* he should do *something*. Feeling deeply odd, Zuko reached out and patted Aang on the shoulder.

“It *itches*,” Aang mumbled.

“Tends to,” Zuko said, “while it’s just growing out. It gets better.”

Aang nodded then immediately shook his head. “It feels *wrong* .”

“Air Nomads keep their heads shaved,” Zuko remembered.

“It’s just… one *more* thing,” Aang said quietly. “It’s hard. Like I’m betraying them.” Zuko left his hand on Aang’s shoulder. The Avatar didn’t seem to want him to take it off, and if Zuko didn’t know any better he’d have said Aang was leaning into it. “I’m the only one left, I should wear my arrow proudly, instead I have to… hide.”

“You have to hide because the Fire Nation is looking for you,” Zuko told him.

“I know that,” Aang muttered into his knee.

“*Because* you’ve been fighting them. Because you didn’t surrender,” Zuko added. He patted Aang’s shoulder again, something in his stomach twisting. “You got this far. It’s only that dangerous because of how much of a danger you pose, how… close you could be to winning.”

Aang tightened his arms around his legs. “Then why does it feel like losing?” He wondered.

“You’re really going to talk about *losing* to me?” Zuko asked him with a snort. “You lost to my sister. When you weren’t even prepared for a fight. So did a bunch of grown men and generals and the so-claimed defenders of Ba Sing Se; if the city had stood with you like they did in the North Pole I think you would have done better.” He looked at Aang carefully, curled up on the floor, suddenly so very small and… child-like. “Ba Sing Se failed *you*, Aang. They stole your bison and ran you around in circles, refusing your help at every turn. You barely had a chance yet you still tried, and you didn't lose anyone you care about. You…” Zuko sighed. “You’re a great Avatar, Aang.”

Aang lifted his head to focus his sad eyes on Zuko, and Zuko winced. “Really?” He asked softly.

“I’m not going to say it again,” Zuko snapped at him.

Aang smiled. “Okay.”

“Look, you…” Zuko felt so uncomfortable his skin was crawling, “you’re fighting back. You can’t rebuild *while* he’s hunting you. If you ran away and hid from him you wouldn’t be *free*, right?”

Aang nodded, though Zuko could tell from a hardening in his jaw that he wasn’t happy about it.

“Having to disguise yourself is one more thing the war took from you,” Zuko said sternly, “but you can make sure it’s the *last*. You can make him pay for it.”

Aang seemed quizzical for a moment, before nodding with a serious look in his eyes. “I think I understand,” he said.

“Good,” Zuko said. *At least one of us does*.

“You’re going to make a great teacher,” Aang said suddenly, his voice light, and bright, and-

“What are you talking about?” Zuko asked him, “My uncle is here.”

“He said he wasn’t going to teach me,” Aang told Zuko, as Zuko felt something like dread sinking in his stomach, “that he was going to help you to teach me instead.”

Zuko stared blankly at him. Sokka might have mentioned something about, but he had *assumed* with his uncle on board that he’d, though, Iroh had only ever had two students- *Zuko*?

Was that actually the best idea? Zuko had never taught anyone before, he hadn’t a single idea where to even *start* . He might know his father’s fighting style well enough, but when it came to the basics of firebending Zuko was *hardly* a master. He wasn’t even close. The Avatar, meanwhile, and Katara, had gone from barely able to bend a snowball to near masters of waterbending in the blink of an eye. It just made more sense for Iroh to train him, for every reason, including the fact Zuko doubted he had the *patience* to teach-

Aang leaned over and wrapped his arms around Zuko’s neck, pulling him into a hug before Zuko knew what he was doing. “Thank you, Zuko,” Aang said into Zuko’s ear.

“*What* are you doing?” Zuko demanded, squirming to free his arms so he could push Aang off.

“A hug,” Aang said happily.

“Stop it.”

“I like to hug my friends,” Aang told Zuko, “and you’re my friend.”

Zuko’s hand stilled on Aang’s shoulder. Then he dropped it with a sigh. “Fine,” he mumbled.

Aang just squeezed him harder and it was… it was alright. Nice, Zuko supposed. They could be friends, Aang wanted to, had wanted to even earlier; Zuko wondered if that was all just Aang, if he trusted Zuko like this because of what Zuko did at the Pohuai Stronghold, or if *Roku* had guided him to do it. If Aang even knew about *that*.

His arms were really small, and he was just so *light* even wrapped around Zuko and leaning on him into the hug. Aang *was* a child. Around the same age Zuko had been when *he’d* faced his father, and soon it was going to be Aang’s turn to do so. Hesitating, Zuko slowly brought his hands to Aang’s shoulders and held him back.

“I guess it went well?”

That was *Sokka*. Zuko snapped his head up to see Sokka standing, grinning, right in front of him. His mind immediately drew a blank.

“Yeah!” Aang said loudly, jumping up from Zuko’s arms with a burst of wind. He landed lightly on his feet and smiled, sheepishly. “It did. Right?”

Zuko looked between the two of them. “Yes?”

Aang turned around, and gave Zuko a bright smile. His shoulders might have still been slumped but he seemed happier. Better. Zuko *had* helped. *Somehow.* “Thanks,” Aang said to him, “for talking to me.”

Swallowing something in his throat, Zuko just nodded. He shifted on the ground, his stomach feeling stiff and tense, and only just managed to catch Sokka’s gaze. Sokka’s left eyebrow lifted slightly. Zuko just held his stomach and shrugged.

“Ugh!” Sokka said, breaking their eye contact as he exaggeratedly stretched his arms over his head. “What a *day*. I don’t know about you, but I’m exhausted.” He brought his arms in front of his chest, using one to stretch the other, cracking his back, and giving Aang a pointed look. “I could use a snack and a nap. What about you, Zuko?”

Zuko smiled softly at him. “That sounds good,” he said, grateful. Nonchalantly, Sokka stepped over, grabbing one of Zuko’s shoulders with one hand and his forearm with the other to help him stand.

“I could use a snack!” Aang said eagerly.

Sokka looked at Zuko. Zuko looked back at him and tried, with everything in his power, to communicate the word ‘*No*’ just with his expression.

Grimacing, Sokka turned his head toward Aang and said apologetically, “Sure, Aang. Sounds fun.”

Aang smiled brightly at them from ear-to-ear. “I’ll go see if Katara and Toph want to join!”

“Great,” Zuko said sourly, “*great*.”

---

There was something in the air that day that seemed determined not to leave him and Sokka alone, as Aang stuck to Zuko’s side like glue until Katara came by to offer a waterbending lesson, immediately after which Iroh appeared with a pai sho set and an annoyingly proud look on his face. If there was anything positive to be said about that afternoon, at least, it was watching the face of his uncle as Sokka achieved his first pai sho victory.

---

The next morning, after Katara and Sokka came by for a session of healing, Katara recommended that Zuko walk a little bit more each day. Sokka seemed delighted by the idea, though he couldn’t have possibly been happier than Zuko, who felt his head twitching with discomfort every hour he had to spend resting in that bed.

Zuko made it up to the deck, and around the perimeter once before his breath was coming in hot and his hands were shaking.

Halfway into a story about the city of Omashu and a crazy king, Sokka put one arm on Zuko’s waist and brought Zuko’s hand over his shoulder. Casually. Like it was a gesture for a regular couple on a romantic walk. Like the presence of the other Southern Water Tribe warriors’ eyes looking at them didn’t matter. Like Zuko didn’t even need to ask for Sokka to help him.

It was a sincere test of will, waiting until they made their painstaking way back to the room for Zuko to kiss him.

---

Katara came by in the middle of the night, stepped over a snoring Iroh, and walked right up to Zuko to whisper to him in a furious hiss that if he hurt her brother again she’d bury him in ice until no amount of blessed spirit water would revive him. Zuko, his inner fire curling in his stomach, stared back at her and couldn’t think of anything to say. *That* response, nothing, was apparently satisfactory enough. She left the room smiling.

When the door shut behind her, Zuko for the very first time was grateful he’d never felt any inclination toward girls. He couldn’t fathom what went on in Katara’s head and didn’t want to try.

---

Iroh was keeping much busier than Zuko, spending mornings with Hakoda and some of the other older warriors discussing their plans, afternoons writing out scrolls of firebending instructions from memory for Zuko, mid afternoons with Aang for some spiritual discussion and tea, and evenings badgering Sokka into another round of pai sho while Zuko glowered at him from the bed.

Zuko was recovering, slowly. Each morning getting a little stronger walking around with Sokka until, a week in, he found he didn’t need Sokka’s assistance on the walk back. He still took it, though, and if Sokka noticed that Zuko wasn’t leaning on him anymore, he didn’t mention it. They did find some time to be alone in the afternoons, when everyone else was busy. Zuko told him about the time he’d been traveling alone, Lee and his family in that desolate Earth Kingdom village, and Sokka told him about some ancient spirit library in the desert that Zuko could barely believe existed.

At some point, when passing Sokka’s father on the deck, Zuko grumbled out a “Good morning, *Chief* Hakoda.”

Hakoda, looking like he was about to laugh, said back, “That seemed like it hurt.”

Zuko had snorted, replied, “It was terrible. *Goodbye*,” and as he’d walked away Zuko heard the sound of several grown men chuckling behind him. Sokka, though, seemed incredibly happy about the effort, so it was worth it.

*Talking* though was more of a formality when they were alone. As if they both knew that’s what they *should* do, ‘get to know each other’, so part of their time *had* to be dedicated to talking. It wasn’t like Zuko didn’t enjoy conversations with Sokka, in fact, he think he liked talking to Sokka more than nearly anything he’d ever done in his life; Sokka was funny, animated, a roundabout storyteller who skipped over boring details and yet could make almost anything interesting, and he always had something to say, it seemed, like the very act of talking was as simple as breathing to him. *However*, time spent curled around each other as if determined to memorize every inch of each other's mouths was just plain superior to anything else. Ever.

If anything, Zuko couldn’t help but wonder if Sokka was about to pull the rug out from him and declare this all a massive joke; though there was absolutely no evidence for it and everything Sokka did seemed nearly designed to prove the opposite. Spending time with Zuko as if he wouldn’t rather be anywhere else, chosing to look over his map and work on that schedule while leaning on Zuko’s shoulder for hours, the way he would casually find Zuko’s hand sometimes, twirling their fingers around casually, a strange kind of intimacy, with thumbs and palms and the way they’d just hold hands when it was probably more convenient not to. Then he’d kiss him, sometimes with an exuberant enthusiasm that would knock Zuko down, sometimes with a serious look on his face like there was a mystery written on Zuko’s face that Sokka was determined to answer.

Though nothing, *nothing*, could compare to the way Sokka’s eyes brightened and he would smile the first time he saw Zuko’s face in the morning. Happy to see him. Happy to recognize him. Happy that *Zuko* was there.

Four days in, a bit later than when they were normally interrupted, Sokka laughed at something he said himself and rolled over onto Zuko, taking both his hands in his. He asked if Zuko *ever* got cold, since he was so warm all the time, and Zuko told him of course he did. Then Sokka leaned forward, kissed Zuko’s forehead, nose, left eye, and the scar, before kissing him on the mouth. Not a difference in one or the other.

Every night since, as Zuko stared up at the ceiling willing himself to sleep, it was the only thing he could think about. Hours spent replaying it over and over again. Sokka’s smile, the stupid excited look in his eyes, and the way he kissed the scar like he didn’t even notice. Or it didn’t matter.

And maybe, Zuko thought, Aang had been a *little* bit right to use *that* word.

---

Zuko spent a good amount of his days attempting to focus and also desperately wishing he could trade whatever remained of his luck so that everyone else would leave him alone besides Sokka. It wasn’t like he didn’t enjoy the others, he and Toph seemed to get alone well, and his relationship with his uncle had entered a strange period where *everything* was easy, natural. Then, of course, he was determined to recover quickly, pushing his body more each day to get back to a place where he could begin firebending training again; with each addition to the scroll Iroh made, and every conversation they had about the upcoming lessons with Aang, Zuko only felt more confident and eager to just get it all over with and start already. Something else though, came crawling into his head whenever he had time to think about it, or was walking along the railing of the ship looking at the ocean passing below. Knowledge. That every hour, every *minute*, was bringing him closer and closer *back home*. That time was limited. That eventually this strange, transitioning period would be over and the urgent work would begin again.

Eleven days in, and the cloak Zuko was wearing was nearly still as the wind was too, though the ship barrelled forward regardless, fueled by coal, Hakoda and the others determined to stick to schedule even if it meant burning more of their resources. He gripped the side of the ship, leaning forward, watching the sun setting in front of him as the ship moved as if to meet him. Heading west.

Zuko wasn’t there for five minutes before Sokka found him.

He walked up to Zuko’s side, put his elbows on the railing, and stood there for a good long while, staring up ahead. Eventually, Sokka turned his head and smiled when he noticed Zuko was watching him. “Hey,” he said.

Zuko nodded.

“Nice night.” Sokka looked back at the horizon.

“Winds are still,” Zuko pointed out.

Sokka chuckled and said, “Yeah. They are.” It was quiet too, like the entire world was waiting. Zuko frowned, narrowing his eyes at the sunset ahead. “So,” Sokka said after a moment, “We’re on our way to the Fire Nation. You’re going back.”

“Yeah,” Zuko turned his head to look at him. Sokka had that serious look on his face, not playful this time. “I guess I am.”

“Hm.” Sokka raised an eyebrow and, reaching out with his elbow, nudged Zuko gently on the arm. “You probably never thought you'd be going home like *this*, though.”

Zuko exhaled deeply. “No,” he said honestly, “Never.”

“Why would you?” Sokka bit his lip. “Is- is that alright?”

Nodding, solemnly, Zuko looked down at his hands. “Everytime before,” he said, “when I thought about returning to the Fire Nation, when I dreamed about it, I- it wasn’t- I didn’t imagine I would be going back as *me*. Who I am. It was always, this *other version* . The son my father always wanted.”

Sokka reached out slowly and took Zuko’s hand. He smiled at him when Zuko’s gaze met his eyes.

“I wanted to be perfect, for him,” Zuko explained quietly, “wanted to be *welcomed home*. I wished-that one day he would *see* me, and miss me. Tell me he regretted sending me away.”

“Hm.” Sokka threaded their fingers together thoughtfully. “Do you think that ever could have happened?”

“No.” Zuko tightened his hand in Sokka’s. “But I used to want it so badly I convinced myself it could. Besides, that version of a son my father always wanted… I think I’d hate him.”

“Sounds like a jerk,” Sokka mused.

“I already tried it. Being perfect for him, playing that role, and I couldn’t do it. No act is flawless, besides I...” Zuko swallowed, ““Even when I dreamed about the best outcomes of the future I don’t think I ever bothered imagining I would be happy.”

“Hm.” Sokka leaned a little closer, his shoulder pressed into Zuko’s side. “Are you… happy now?”

“Yes,” Zuko told him simply.

“Good to know,” Sokka said with a twinkle in his eye. Zuko nodded, then leaned over until his head was resting on Sokka’s shoulder. Comfortable. “So,” Sokka said, sounding amused, “Do you remember a bit back? When you said you didn’t want to be a part of my stupid team?”

*When had*- oh. In the woods by Lake Laogai, right after Zuko had left his uncle. “Yeah,” Zuko said, still leaning on him.

“Well, well,” Sokka said with a chuckle, “look who ate his words.”

“Guess I did,” Zuko admitted. He squeezed Sokka’s hand once, and then Sokka’s head dipped down enough to be resting on Zuko’s shoulder too. It was nice. Casual. Comfortable. *Calming*. Some of that anxiety, roiling around in Zuko’s stomach, eased.

Zuko looked up at the bright blue sky as a grateful feeling spread over him like the warmth of a fire. There was still a long way to go and so much to do, but now, beyond any measure of doubt, Zuko knew he wasn’t alone.
